models_evaluated: Institutional rule-based VTE chemoprophylaxis interruptive CDS alert

links.outcome: Alert firing frequency during silent testing before release
links.effect: Silent testing showed the initial alert fired an average of 11,154 times per week, prompting significant logic refinements before release.
links.quote: The initial alert fired an average of 11,154 times per week when tested silently, prompting significant refinements before release.

links.outcome: Alert dismissal without orders after iterative logic changes
links.effect: Alert dismissed without further action 88% of the time; modifications did not significantly decrease dismissal; firing rose from 53.8 to 61 per 1,000 patient days.
links.quote: Modifications also did not cause a significant decrease in how frequently the alert was dismissed without further action being taken (88%).

unlisted_practices: Classifying narrative user feedback into themes (e.g., 'wrong person' receiving alert) to drive iterative alert logic revision

links.outcome: Alert dismissal without further action after iterative corrective modifications
links.effect: Modifications did not significantly decrease dismissal without further action (88%).
links.quote: Modifications also did not cause a significant decrease in how frequently the alert was dismissed without further action being taken (88%).

links.outcome: Workflow mismatch reflected in negative user feedback
links.effect: The wrong person receiving the alert accounted for nearly 50% of negative submitted user feedback, despite logic intended to target the patient's primary team.
links.quote: Review of narrative feedback and its classification highlights "wrong person" receiving the alert being by far the most prevalent cause for negative submitted user feedback (nearly 50%), despite efforts to develop logic that limits firing to the patient's primary team.

unlisted_practices: Restrict interruptive alerts to the patient's primary team through recipient-targeting logic.

links.effect: The initial alert fired 11,154 times per week during silent testing, leading to significant pre-release refinements.
links.quote: The initial alert fired an average of 11,154 times per week when tested silently, prompting significant refinements before release.

links.effect: Post-launch modifications based on feedback did not significantly decrease the 88% rate of alerts being dismissed without action.
links.quote: Modifications also did not cause a significant decrease in how frequently the alert was dismissed without further action being taken (88%).
